item.title: Chinese vice premier urges steadily advancing rural revitalization
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
LANZHOU, Nov. 19 -- Chinese Vice Premier Liu Guozhong has called for consolidating poverty alleviation achievements, preventing large-scale relapse into poverty, and steadily advancing rural revitalization across the board. Liu, who is also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks during a research tour from Monday to Thursday in northwest China's Gansu Province. He chaired a symposium on regular assistance work in five provinces and autonomous regions in northwest China. In Longnan's Tanchang County, Wenxian County and Wudu District, Liu inspected the monitoring system to prevent relapse into poverty, industrial and employment assistance, east-west collaboration, and targeted assistance by central government agencies. This year marks the first year of implementing regular assistance. Efforts must be made to carry out all related policies and measures in a meticulous and thorough manner, and continue to improve the lives of rural residents, he said. It is necessary to promote the upgrading of assistance industries in accordance with local conditions, strengthen skills training and labor cooperation, and spare no effort to expand employment channels, Liu noted. Also, work should be done to develop the county-level economy and help accelerate the development of old revolutionary base areas, ethnic minority areas and border areas, he said. The vice premier, in addition, stressed applying the experience gained from the Green Rural Revival Program in Zhejiang Province in east China to build a beautiful and harmonious countryside that is desirable to live and work in.

item.title: Chinese vice premier to visit Singapore
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
BEIJING, Nov. 20 -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang will visit Singapore from November 22 to 23 at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister of Singapore Gan Kim Yong, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Friday. Ding, member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, will co-chair with Gan bilateral cooperation mechanism meetings, the spokesperson said. The meetings include the 22nd meeting of the China-Singapore Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation, the 27th meeting of the China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park Joint Steering Council, the 18th meeting of the China-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City Joint Steering Council, and the 10th meeting of the China-Singapore (Chongqing) Demonstration Initiative on Strategic Connectivity Joint Steering Council, according to the spokesperson.

item.title: Xi, Prabowo announce launch of China-Indonesia comprehensive economic partnership negotiations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto on Friday announced the launch of negotiations for a bilateral comprehensive economic partnership. The announcement was made during Xi's meeting with Prabowo in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Prabowo is in China for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. Xi said the two countries should strengthen strategic communication and solidarity, deepen all-round strategic cooperation, consolidate the foundation of political trust, and jointly guard against and respond to external risks. He called on both countries to expand mutually beneficial cooperation, advance major projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, and deepen cooperation in energy and mineral resources, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, and clean energy. Xi called for efforts to reach an all-round, high-standard comprehensive economic partnership agreement at an early date. Amid emerging risks and challenges in the world, China is ready to strengthen coordination and cooperation with Indonesia within multilateral frameworks, including the United Nations, APEC and China-ASEAN cooperation, Xi said. Prabowo said Indonesia's strategic partnership with China is stronger than ever, reaffirming that Indonesia firmly adheres to the one-China policy and that Taiwan is a province of the People's Republic of China. Indonesia sincerely welcomes Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in the country, and is committed to providing a reliable, stable and predictable business environment, Prabowo said. Prabowo said Indonesia highly appreciates China's role as a responsible major country in international affairs, and stands ready to work with China to safeguard the shared interests of the Global South and promote regional and global peace and stability.

item.title: Xi says China, Singapore should strengthen strategic communication, enhance coordination
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Friday that China and Singapore should strengthen strategic communication and enhance solidarity and coordination as the world is undergoing accelerated changes unseen in a century. The two countries should be sincere friends who trust each other and support each other in pursuing development paths suited to their respective national conditions, said Xi when meeting with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Wong attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held from Wednesday to Thursday in Shenzhen. During the meeting, Xi called for advancing the all-round high-quality future-oriented partnership between China and Singapore to new heights, and stressed the need for both sides to advance high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. The two countries should launch negotiations for upgraded Version 4.0 of their free trade agreement, and deliver signature cooperation outcomes in areas such as the digital economy, green development, and artificial intelligence, Xi added. Noting that both countries should be "a progressive force" for championing international fairness and justice, Xi called for safeguarding regional peace and stability while jointly building an Asia-Pacific community and a community with a shared future for humanity. For his part, Wong stated that Singapore firmly adheres to the one-China policy and opposes "Taiwan independence." Singapore stands ready to work with China to enhance political mutual trust, deepen cooperation in areas such as trade, industrial and supply chains, and artificial intelligence, and promote people-to-people exchanges, the prime minister noted. Wong said Singapore is willing to strengthen communication and cooperation with the Chinese side on international affairs to jointly address global challenges.

item.title: Xi calls for promoting building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to higher level
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Friday called for promoting the building of a China-Thailand community with a shared future to a higher level. China and Thailand should continuously enhance political mutual trust and strengthen solidarity and coordination, Xi said when meeting with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. The two countries should step up exchanges between governments, political parties, legislatures and at other levels, and safeguard their common strategic interests, Xi stressed. He called on the two sides to make good use of cooperation mechanisms in economy and trade, science and technology, and the digital economy, expand and strengthen traditional cooperation in agriculture and connectivity, and cultivate and strengthen new growth areas of cooperation such as artificial intelligence, new energy vehicles, aviation and aerospace, disaster prevention, mitigation and relief, and water resources management. The two sides should strengthen cooperation in culture, education, and tourism, Xi added. He also urged intensifying efforts to crack down on illegal and criminal activities such as online gambling and telecom fraud. The two sides should strengthen multilateral coordination and work together to safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Xi said. China is ready to play a positive role in bringing about an early turnaround in Thailand-Cambodia relations, Xi said. For his part, Anutin said Thailand is ready to continue to strengthen high-level exchanges with China and enhance cooperation in areas such as trade, investment, science and technology, industrial and supply chains, and connectivity. Thailand will resolutely crack down on cross-border crimes including online gambling and telecom fraud, and protect the safety of Chinese citizens in Thailand, he said, adding that the country welcomes more Chinese visitors. Anutin attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, held from Wednesday to Thursday.

item.title: Xi says China ready for closer cooperation with Malaysia
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 -- China stands ready to foster greater momentum for cooperation with Malaysia to bring more benefits to people of both countries, President Xi Jinping said Friday. China-Malaysia relations have maintained high-level development since the two sides reached important consensus on building a high-level strategic China-Malaysia community with a shared future and ushered in a new "Golden 50 Years" for bilateral ties in April last year, he said. Xi made the remarks when meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. China and Malaysia should maintain high-level strategic communication and support each other in safeguarding their respective national sovereignty, security and development interests, Xi said at the meeting. The two sides should also ensure high-quality development and operation of key projects, expand and improve agricultural product trade, and broaden cooperation in tourism, education and other areas, he added. Xi called for joint efforts to advance the reform of global governance, strengthen coordination and cooperation within multilateral frameworks such as APEC, and safeguard the common interests of developing countries. Anwar said the Taiwan question is China's internal affair, and Malaysia firmly adheres to the one-China policy. He said Malaysia is ready to strengthen strategic coordination with China, give full play to the role of bilateral cooperation mechanisms, ensure the sound operation of key infrastructure projects, and enhance cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence. Malaysia will also promote inter-civilization exchanges and dialogue, step up coordination and collaboration in international affairs, and keep elevating the level of Malaysia-China relations, Anwar said. Anwar attended the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting held from Wednesday to Thursday in Shenzhen.

item.title: Xi says China, Australia should be mutually trusted partners
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-20
SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Friday that China and Australia should be cooperative partners who trust each other and help each other succeed, as the two countries have no historical grievances or conflicts of fundamental interests. China-Australia relations are stable at present, said Xi when meeting with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Albanese is in China for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held from Wednesday to Thursday. As next year marks the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and Australia, Xi called on the two sides to achieve greater progress in bilateral relations from a new starting point. Xi said that in a volatile and turbulent world, the two countries should enhance mutual trust, accommodate each other's core interests and major concerns, and keep to the right direction of friendship and cooperation. He called for deepening mutually beneficial cooperation in pursuit of the two countries' respective development goals, advancing traditional cooperation in agriculture, energy and minerals, and expanding cooperation in emerging areas such as the green economy, new energy, the digital industry, artificial intelligence (AI) and climate change response. Efforts should be made to promote friendship between the two countries through expanded people-to-people exchanges, Xi said, noting that the two sides had agreed to designate 2027 as the China-Australia Year of Tourism. He also emphasized the need to strengthen multilateral coordination in addressing global challenges, advance the building of an Asia-Pacific community, and jointly uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order based on international law. Albanese said that the improvement and development of Australia-China relations serves the interests of both sides and brings tangible benefits to the peoples of both countries. He said that Australia stands ready to maintain close high-level exchanges with China, strengthen practical cooperation in trade, investment, AI and other areas, deepen people-to-people exchanges, respect each other and properly handle differences, so as to make Australia-China relations an example for countries with different systems to develop constructive relations.

item.title: Xi chairs APEC meeting, calls for building Asia-Pacific community
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the "Asia-Pacific miracle." "We must strive to build an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development," Xi said as he chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18-19. Xi noted that for more than three decades, the Asia-Pacific region has undergone tremendous changes, creating the "Asia-Pacific miracle" of rapid economic growth. In the face of new opportunities and challenges, the region must adapt to the new realities and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation, he added. Xi called for solidarity and mutual assistance in building an Asia-Pacific community, urging APEC economies to expand their shared interests, meet the difficulties and challenges together, and steadily foster a shared sense of community. "Members of APEC are like passengers riding the same ship. To navigate the waves of the Pacific, we must unite as one and look out for each other," he said. Xi highlighted the importance of openness and integration, calling for efforts to uphold open regionalism, steadily advance economic integration, and champion free and open trade and investment, while developing a cooperation pattern that is open and integrated rather than exclusive or fragmented. Building an Asia-Pacific community requires enterprise and innovation, Xi said, urging stronger scientific and technological cooperation, the commercialization of innovation outcomes, and an open, fair, just and nondiscriminatory environment for cooperation. He also underscored the importance of inclusive development, stressing the need to ensure that development benefits all, deliver for the people, and foster favorable conditions for turning the vision of an Asia-Pacific community into reality. FOUR PILLARS Founded in 1989, APEC now brings together 21 member economies, including China, Russia and the United States. China joined in 1991. The forum has helped expand trade and investment and strengthen economic ties across the region. "China has been an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation," Xi said at the Shenzhen meeting, adding that the country is ready to work with all parties to build the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community -- economy and trade, connectivity, innovation, and development. The Chinese president called for stronger economy and trade as a pillar underpinning such a community. Efforts should be made to align various regional economic and trade agreements, boost trade and investment facilitation and digitalization, and reduce barriers to trade and investment, he said. Xi underscored the importance of upgrading connectivity in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called for measures to improve infrastructure network, harmonize policies and regulations, advance people-to-people exchanges, and promote mutual understanding and closer bonds among peoples. Innovation should be fostered as another pillar of the Asia-Pacific community, Xi said. Greater efforts need to be made to develop digital infrastructure and encourage the broad application of artificial intelligence, he added. Xi also stressed the importance of development in building the Asia-Pacific community. He called on regional economies to advance cooperation on energy and food security, anti-corruption governance across borders, and green and low-carbon transition. He also expressed support for improving the people's well-being and called for increased investment in human capital. TURNING CONSENSUS INTO ACTION China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, Xi said. He announced that China would contribute 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC practical cooperation. China will also establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges, and set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises, according to Xi. Leaders and representatives of APEC member economies shared their views at the meeting on building an Asia-Pacific community to prosper together. They spoke highly of the achievements of China's APEC host year and expressed their readiness to step up cooperation to advance APEC's development. In his closing remarks, Xi called for strengthening confidence to translate the consensus on building an Asia-Pacific community into concrete action, and to turn the vision into reality. He stressed the need to focus on development as the broadest common ground for cooperation and deliver more tangible benefits through Asia-Pacific cooperation. The meeting adopted by consensus the 2026 APEC Leaders' Declaration, which sets out the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, and three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation. Vietnam took over as APEC host for 2027, with President To Lam inviting leaders and representatives of member economies to attend next year's meeting in Vietnam. Full text: Remarks by Chinese President Xi Jinping at the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting

item.title: Chinese premier urges China, ASEAN to stand united, overcome distractions
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
MANILA, Nov. 16 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang said on Monday that in a turbulent and complex world, China and ASEAN should stand united, overcome distractions and work together to build a closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future. Li made the remarks during the 29th China-ASEAN Summit in Manila. As this year marks the fifth anniversary of the establishment of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, Li said that over the past five years, the world has witnessed a growing trend of unilateralism and protectionism, while geopolitical conflicts have flared up one after another. Against this backdrop, China-ASEAN cooperation has forged ahead, achieving both quantitative growth and qualitative improvements, with cooperation mechanisms further consolidated and connectivity steadily enhanced, he said. The extraordinary five years and the hard-won achievements offer valuable experience and useful lessons, Li said. He stressed that both sides need to carry forward their tradition of friendship and mutual assistance, uphold the right path of openness and win-win cooperation, and keep pace with the trend of innovation and development. These experiences and lessons are a valuable asset shared by both sides and should be upheld and put to full use over the long term, Li said. Five years ago, Chinese President Xi Jinping proposed that China and ASEAN work together to build a peaceful, safe and secure, prosperous, beautiful and amicable home, Li said, adding that both China and ASEAN countries cherish the culture of family and are geographically close and bound by strong people-to-people ties. The profound bonds forged over generations should not, and will not, be affected by temporary events or circumstances, he said. Li urged China and ASEAN countries to protect and develop their common home, injecting greater stability and certainty into the development and prosperity of the global village. He called on the two sides to strengthen the foundations for peace and security by properly handling differences through dialogue and consultation, jointly opposing external interference, and safeguarding regional peace and stability. China looks forward to the early conclusion of the Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea, which will provide a solid institutional guarantee for lasting peace and stability in the South China Sea, Li said. He also called for promoting regional development and prosperity, stressing the need for both sides to take the entry into force of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area (FTA) 3.0 Upgrade Protocol as an opportunity to deepen industrial and supply chain cooperation, accelerate infrastructure connectivity, or "hard connectivity," in areas such as railways and highways, and strengthen "soft connectivity" in mechanisms, standards and rules. The premier said China applauds the establishment of a China-ASEAN mechanism for energy ministers' meetings and stands ready to work with ASEAN to successfully hold the China-ASEAN Year of artificial intelligence (AI) cooperation next year, advance "AI+" cooperation and create a strong engine for high-quality regional economic development. Li also called for improving the well-being of the people, voicing China's readiness to continue to contribute to the China-ASEAN Cooperation Fund and strengthen cooperation with ASEAN in areas including poverty reduction, disaster prevention and mitigation, food security, maternal and child health, so as to promote sustainable development in the region. Commending the fruitful outcomes achieved over the five years since the establishment of the ASEAN-China comprehensive strategic partnership, leaders of ASEAN countries expressed readiness to strengthen strategic communication and political mutual trust with China, fully implement the ASEAN-China FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, and deepen cooperation in areas including economy and trade, connectivity, AI, clean energy, digital economy and combating transnational crime. They thanked China for its consistent support for ASEAN centrality in the regional architecture and its commitment to the peaceful settlement of disputes. They also expressed the hope for an early conclusion of the COC in the South China Sea, jointly safeguarding regional peace and stability, and building an ASEAN-China community with a shared future. It was announced during the meeting that the China-ASEAN FTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol will enter into force on Dec. 1, 2026, and 2027 has been designated as the Year of AI cooperation. Outcome documents were released, covering the 5th anniversary of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership, energy partnership building, and deeper forestry cooperation. Full Text: Remarks by Chinese Premier Li Qiang at the 29th China-ASEAN Summit
